title: oven-braised mexican chicken dumplings
description: A rich, spicy, and slightly sweet Mexican-inspired dish featuring poached chicken and homemade yeasty dumplings.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs

instructions: In a small bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until the yeast is activated and foamy.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and spices. Add the yeast mixture and mix until a shaggy dough forms.

Knead the dough for 10-15 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. Place it in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the chicken. Poach the chicken for 10-12 minutes, or until it is cooked through.
While the chicken is cooking, mix the sherry vinegar, cumin, paprika, and cayenne pepper in a small bowl.
Once the chicken is done, remove it from the water and let it cool slightly. Shred or chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface to a thickness of about 1/4 inch. Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of the chicken mixture onto one half of each dough circle. Fold the dough over the filling and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Place the dumplings on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Brush the tops with the vegetable oil.
Bake the dumplings in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until they are golden brown and puffed.
Remove the dumplings from the oven and let them cool for a few minutes. Brush the tops with the sherry vinegar mixture and serve hot.
